newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK red-chip fever pushes value of bank shares.
newsitem.headline: HK red-chip fever pushes value of bank shares.

text.p: China-related banks have become the latest Hong Kong market sector to feel the heat of red-chip fever, which is pushing bank shares to new highs.

But investors are asking how one values a rapidly growing bank in an emerging economy that is undergoing slow but steady financial reform, but where credit assessment and accounting systems are very different from Western models.
If that bank is operating in China, the answer appears to lie anywhere between five and 50 times earnings, analysts said.

"I would value a red-chip bank a bit higher than Hong Kong's small and medium-sized banks," said Alex Wong, banking analyst at Dharmala Securities. "But not as high as sector leaders Hang Seng Bank and Bank of East Asia".
The market average for the share price of small and medium-sized banks is 13-14 times 1996 earnings. Hang Seng Bank is trading on 20 times and Bank of East Asia 28 times.

But market speculators chasing red-chip banks are looking for asset injections from a wealthy China-based parent, not standard valuations. Red chips are Hong Kong shares of companies with strong Chinese backing.

"The whole red-chip story is all about asset injections," said Keith Irving, banking analyst at Merrill Lynch. "If the company has a major mainland parent, it has a much better chance of getting mainland assets injected into it."
The latest target of the red-chip asset-injection craze is China Everbright IHD Pacific Ltd.

Shares of Everbright IHD soared to an all-time high of HK$12.05 on Friday. It ended at HK$11.90, up 14.71 percent on the day. At the close, the share was trading on a price-earnings (P/E) ratio of 922 times March 1996 earnings.

The rise followed a company statement which said proposed acquisitions under consideration included a possible acquisition of equity interest in Beijing-based Everbright Bank of China, a unit of ultimate parent the China Everbright Group.
But it stressed no negotiations whatsoever have been conducted in connection with such an acquisition.
Analysts cautioned an independent assessment of a bank's balance sheet, including its loan book, was needed to determine its proper market price.
But a simplistic valuation could use the price the Asian Development Bank and others paid for a stake in Everbright Bank, said one analyst with a U.S. brokerage firm.

In January, the ADB and 131 other shareholders took up 49 percent, or 1.37 billion shares, of the bank at 1.80 yuan per share. Based on 1996 earnings per share of 0.318 yuan, China's first joint stock bank was priced on an historic P/E of 5.66 times.
China Everbright IHD already holds a 20 percent stake in a Hong Kong bank, International Bank of Asia Ltd (IBA) which it acquired from its parent company in January.

Despite the connection, shares in IBA have fallen steadily since the acquisition, rising only in latest wave of red chip mania in May. On Friday, the share closed HK$0.10 higher at HK$5.65, giving a historic P/E of 9.94 times.

Ka Wah Bank Ltd, which is 61.3 percent held by Beijing-based China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC), rose to a year high of HK$4.50 on Friday. The share closed at HK$4.35, but at a P/E of just 13 times 1996 earnings.
Union Bank of Hong Kong Ltd, 60 percent held by China Merchants Holdings Co Ltd, recently hit an all-time high of HK$14.70, putting this small, red-chip bank on nearly 13 times 1996 earnings.
The HKCB Bank Holding Co Ltd, which is connected with China Resources (Holdings) Co Ltd, has leaped more than 100 percent to a new high of HK$5.60 and a P/E of nearly 20 times in the past month.

The only listed benchmark for valuing a domestic China bank is Shenzhen Development Bank which has A shares listed in Shenzhen. This is Shenzhen's premier blue chip and it has always traded at a premium to the market, analysts said.
The bank reported net profits of 787.5 million yuan in 1996, an 81 percent increase over the previous year, and total assets of 30.02 billion yuan, an increase of 47.80 percent.
Despite its name, the bank appears to function much like a commercial bank rather than a policy bank, and its share price reflects this more aggressive mandate.
As at the close of Friday, the share was trading on a price earning multiple of more than 50 times 1996 earnings.
